newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel seen testing $25 support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel seen testing $25 support.

text.p: Singapore gas oil traded at $25.50 per barrel on Friday and was expected to test the $25.00 support level soon as a Singapore trader steadily lowered its purchase price, traders said.
The $25.00 level has been the support since end-January when gas oil value fell from a high of over $32.00 in early January.

Traders said the market has been fundamentally soft for about a month now amid weak regional demand but has received support at over $26.00 due to a buying spree by the Singapore trader and its related company.
About 12 offers were seen in the market, indicating that the market remains well-supplied, traders said.

The softer market on Friday, which saw prices for May cargoes falling by about 80 cents per barrel from Wednesday, was also exacerbated by India's surprising purchase of only six 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil cargoes totalling 270,000 tonnes for June deliveries.
The market had expected India to take 600,000 tonnes in this tender.
A Singapore trader bought another 300,000 barrels in two cargoes at $25.50 one from a French refiner for May 17-21 lifting and another from a Swiss trader for May 27-31.
The Swiss trader who still has large volumes of unsold arbitrage cargoes, sold another cargo to a Japanese trader at $25.50 for May 17-21 lifting.
The physical price for May has flattened to the same level.

Traders said the market might test the $25.00 support on Monday if the Singapore traders, who have bought over 18 million barrels, press prices further downwards on Monday and more sellers emerged to take up their bid.

"The traders want to buy cheaper oil now. They could be there on Monday to press prices down by another 50 cents," one trader said. "Not all sellers are very desperate today but if everyone else are prepared to sell lower, the market could go down further."
Traders noted that gas oil values were sliding to almost the same level as jet fuel which was offered at $25.40-$25.50 per barrel, and bid at $25.00-$25.30 for end May early June lifting.
This prompted the swaps jet fuel regrade for May to switch from negative to positive level at flat to 25 cents per barrel, while June regrade widened to 65/85 cents.
The bearish sentiment on physical gas oil rubbed on to the swaps market that lost 50 cents for May and 40 cents for June.
